argument_summary: The certification defense should be read narrowly. The admissible record supports launch readiness on aggregate grounds because the current release clears readiness by 2.4 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance supports ongoing measurement, monitoring, and transparent documentation of limitations. The packet does not support a claim of clean present compliance. It supports only a caveated certification posture in which the current-release record must expressly carry the subgroup weakness by disclosure or equivalent approved mitigation coverage, because that is the policy predicate the evidence identifies.
claims_about_policy: The policy point is not disputed. Current-release documentation must reflect current evaluation results, and a material segment weakness for a named launch use case must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Prior approval and informal monitoring are contextual only. The actor position is therefore a narrowed one: the packet is not claiming that prior approval or aggregate readiness overrides the policy predicate; it is claiming that certification is supportable only as caveated compliance tied to that predicate.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is relied upon here. Launch velocity and escalation cost are not offered as policy substitutes and should not control the compliance determination.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence in this record that current-release disclosure language or an approved mitigation record is already attached.
The health-plan benefits support subgroup regression is a real current-release weakness in the admissible record.
Prior approval from nine weeks earlier and the informal post-launch monitoring comment do not by themselves satisfy the stated policy requirement.
A clean-compliance characterization would be overbroad on the present record.
